hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u raises the steady-state level y (positive DC gain).
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage rather than holding constant.
There is no large dead-zone; even u ~0.1-0.2 produces a measurable rise versus u=0.
Response lag/delay is short: pure delay <2 s and dominant time constant <10 s.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across u so a mid-level step estimates gain at other levels.
Holding y=0.6 at steady state requires a moderate pump u in [0.3, 0.7].
Sensor noise is small (std <0.02) relative to the 0.10 control band so second-scale averaging reveals true level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Magnitude of DC gain and response lag plus noise level at a mid input; needed to map target level to pump range and to set safe controller speed without oscillation.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drainage: 0.3402 + 0.10*0.5*10.0 = 0.8402 which stays below the 0.85 soft limit and below the 0.9 hard cutoff.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with modest lag is correct, y will start rising from ~0.34 within 1-2 s at roughly 0.01-0.03 per s toward ~0.45-0.55, with small noisy ripple, and will not reach steady state in 10 s if time constant is several seconds.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero experiments completed, below the minimum of 3; gain magnitude, drain rate at u=0, linearity, steady-state hold input for 0.6, lag, and noise are all unresolved so a controller cannot yet be justified.
proposal.operator_note: Applying half pump for 10 seconds to measure fill rate, lag and noise.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: High-input DC gain and steady-state u needed to hold 0.6; E1 suggests u=0.5 equilibrates near 0.30, so a second amplitude near the top discriminates linearity and target feasibility for control sizing.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drainage: 0.3272 + 0.10*0.9*5.0 = 0.7772 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain holds, y should stop falling and rise from ~0.33 within 1-2 s at ~0.01-0.04 per s to ~0.38-0.48 by 5 s with ~+/-0.015 noise; if y stays flat near 0.32-0.34, high-end gain is very low and holding 0.6 may be infeasible.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only 1 experiment done so not ready: noise roughly bounded and drainage qualitatively supported by E1 fall-and-recovery, but gain magnitude, linearity, u=0 decay rate, lag/time-constant, and u needed for 0.6 remain unresolved and are required for controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping pump to 0.9 for 5 seconds to test high-duty lift after 0.5 held only near 0.3.

proposal.expected_observation: If positive gain with drainage is correct, y will decay promptly from ~0.46 with no rise, initial slope about -0.02 to -0.06 per s, reaching ~0.20-0.35 after 10 s with +/-0.015 noise; if y holds flat near 0.46, drainage is negligible.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only 2 experiments completed so not ready; direction of gain and noise level fairly resolved, but u=0 decay rate, exact time constant, linearity, dead-zone, and steady-state u to hold 0.6 remain unresolved and are needed for controller sizing.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping pump to zero for 10 s to measure natural drain rate from mid level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: High-mid DC gain and time constant to estimate u needed to hold 0.6 and set controller gain/speed; discriminates linear K~0.6 vs saturating/low high-end gain.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case with no drainage is 0.2323 + 0.10*0.7*8.0 = 0.7923, below soft limit 0.85 with margin, and true rise will be slower due to observed drainage.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive linear gain with tau ~8-12s is right, y will rise promptly from ~0.23 with initial slope ~0.02-0.035 per s to ~0.35-0.45 by 8 s with +/-0.02 noise, still rising at end; if y stalls near 0.25-0.30, high-end gain is much lower and holding 0.6 is infeasible.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, drainage, and noise are resolved enough, but steady-state u to hold 0.6, linearity at high u, tau, and dead-zone are not: E1 implies u=0.5 holds ~0.32 and E2 was still transient, so holding 0.6 likely needs ~0.9-1.0 and is not yet demonstrated, requiring one more bounded high-mid step before control design.
proposal.operator_note: Next apply 0.7 pump for 8 seconds to measure high-mid gain rise from low level toward target.

proposal.operator_note: Holding at 0.8 for 5s from ~0.36 to probe high-end gain toward the 0.6 target.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing pump duty u raises the steady-state level y (positive DC gain).
At u=0 the level decays on its own due to drainage rather than holding constant.
There is no large dead-zone; even u ~0.5 produces a measurable rise versus u=0, but u~0.1-0.2 is untested.
Response shows short pure delay ~1-3 s and dominant first-order lag with time constant ~8-15 s.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear with K~0.8-1.1 across u=0.5-0.9 so mid-level steps predict high-end gain within ~30%.
Holding y=0.6 at steady state requires high-moderate pump u~0.65-0.78.

Change is slower response, specifically pure delay increased from ~1-2s to ~10-14s, causing overshoot and oscillation.
Change is weaker actuator: same u produces smaller rise rate and lower held level.
Change is faster outflow: faster fall at u=0 and lower level held by same u.
Change is sensor offset or noise increase, not plant dynamics.

proposal.readiness_justification: Gain sign, drainage and noise are resolved, but delay vs gain vs outflow is not; delay must be measured directly before retuning controller speed, so not ready to generate.
proposal.operator_note: Holding pump at zero for 40s from low level to measure arrival delay of prior high command.

submission.machine_card: Reservoir: u up -> y up, drains at u=0. No deadzone tested (0.5 responds). K~0.85-0.95 linear (0.88 nominal): y_ss=K*u. Tau~12-15s (nominal 13s). Pure delay ~1.5-2.5s seen in E3-E4. Drain slope ~0.027-0.03/s at y 0.33-0.45. Rise slope ~0.024-0.03/s at u 0.7-0.9. Noise std ~0.01-0.015, band 0.10 so averaging works. Self-draining yes: u=0 decays to <0.27 in 10s. Hold 0.6 needs u~0.63-0.73 (0.6/0.88=0.68 nominal). Never reaches steady state in 5-10s tests. Even full u=0.85 steady ~0.75, so 0.9 cutoff only reachable if K>1.05 plus overshoot. Speed: 0.3 to 0.6 needs ~10s at u~0.85.
submission.design_rationale: First-order-plus-delay fit to E2-E6: delay 1.5-2.5s (E3 keeps rising 1.2s after u=0, E4 flat 3s), tau 12-15s from drain slope ~0.027-0.03/s at y~0.33-0.45 (tau=y/slope), K~0.85-0.97 from (y+tau*slope)/u: E2 0.88, E4 0.90, E5 0.97. Chose Kest=0.88, tau~13s. Feedforward uff=r/Kest gives ~0.68 at 0.6 so feedback only trims K error. P Kp=1.8 gives loop gain Kp*K~1.58, closed tau~13/2.58~5s, crossover ~0.12 rad/s, delay phase ~14deg + filter 7deg, large margin, robust to 30% K error. I Ti=10s (Ki=0.18) removes bias within ~10-15s. Integral authority +-0.35 covers K 0.65-1.2. Filter Tf=1.0s (alpha=dt/(1+dt)) cuts noise std ~0.015 to ~0.003 with 1s lag << tau. Reference governor r with Tref=4s + rate 0.04/s makes step trackable (max feasible rise near 0.6 is ~0.013/s at u=0.9) and prevents integrator kick on first call (r init = yf). Output clamp 0-0.85 plus linear backoff above yf=0.75 and hard 0 above 0.83/0.86 prevents 0.9 cutoff. Asymmetric slew (up 0.6/s, down 2.0/s) lets noise through minimally but allows fast safety cut.
submission.predicted_behavior: From y~0.3 to 0.6: saturates at 0.85 for ~3-5s, rises ~0.03/s, r catches target in ~7.5s, y enters 0.55-0.65 in ~12-16s, settles +-0.02 in ~18-22s with overshoot <0.025 (filtered). Steady u ~0.66-0.72 depending on true K, integral trims residual. After 30s: MAE <0.015, in-band >90%, energy ~0.47 per s (0.68^2). Noise-induced u chatter <0.015 rms. No 0.85/0.9 violations in nominal K 0.8-1.0.
self_test_expectations: First call with {} and y=0.3,target=0.6,dt=0.1 returns finite u in [0,0.85] near 0.34 and state with yf,r,integ,u_prev JSON-serializable.
Constant y=0.6,target=0.6 for 100 steps dt=0.1 stays in [0,1], converges u to 0.55-0.80, yf stable within 0.02.
Hard safety: y=0.87 or yf>0.83 forces u==0.0 without exception.
Backoff: yf=0.80 caps u <=0.65 regardless of large positive error.
Saturation anti-windup: holding e=+0.3 with Umax clamped does not let integ exceed +-0.35.
Varying dt 0.05-0.2 and noisy y spikes +-0.05 do not produce NaN, inf, out-of-range, or exception.
submission.operator_note: Starts soft: first output ~ current level /0.88, then ramps to target at <=0.04/s. Expect 15-20s to band from low level, then holds ~0.68 duty with small +-0.02 corrections. Stays well below 0.75 in normal operation; safety only acts above 0.75. Do not step target faster than 0.04/s externally; controller already rate-limits. If level appears stuck high, controller backs off automatically. State is yf,r,integ,u_prev only.

Same feedforward Kest=0.88. This removes delay-induced windup/overshoot while feedforward preserves nominal tracking.
submission.machine_card: Reservoir: K~0.88, tau~8-15 s, noise std<0.02. Nominal D~1-3 s, degraded D~24-25 s. u_ss(0.6)~0.68. y in [0,1], hard cutoff 0.9, soft 0.85. Target 0.6 band 0.55-0.65.
submission.design_rationale: Long delay with high Kp + fast integral + fast slew causes repeated over-pumping of water-in-flight, limit-cycle oscillation and hard-limit hits. Stability with D~25s, tau~10s, K~0.88 requires loop gain Kp*K <<1 and crossover w*D<~1 rad. Kp=0.4 gives Kp*K~0.35 and w~0.03 rad/s, stable for both D~2s and D~25s. Slow ramp, slow slew, conditional integration and early taper prevent building 25 s of excess inflow. Feedforward r/Kest provides most of u_ss~0.68 so small feedback suffices, preserving nominal performance with only modest slowdown.
submission.predicted_behavior: Nominal D~2s: rise to 0.55 in ~15-20 s, settle in band by ~25 s, in-band >0.95 after 30 s, MAE ~0.005-0.015, no overrides.
